game_name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition

verdict.tagline: Endless open exploration tempered by clunky mechanics and bugs.
for_you_if: you want massive open worlds to explore
you plan to mod the experience heavily
not_for_you_if: you need modern fluid combat systems

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players note technical annoyances involving hardware inputs early on.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that connected controllers interfere with mouse and keyboard inputs, requiring players to unplug the controller or disable it to regain normal control.

citations.review_text: For some reason, Skyrim thinks I am playing on Xbox; there are no mouse and keyboard settings  or pc settings

F*(! the devs for locking exclusive priority of keyboard keys.
I can not use any of the shortcuts or any of the windows keys.
PrntSc, Windows, alt+f4, all of them do not work and finding a fix is surprisingly a futile adventure. Try to disable gamepad in Skyrim.ini, install fixes from nexusmods, install collections, none of them work.

Though, in main menu of the game everything works, but when you press "Continue", it stops working.
Hey, I have a controller.  Doesn't mean I want to use it.  Can't control this game unless I unplug said controller.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Reviewers note dated graphics alongside combat system limitations and mod instability.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game's graphics and mechanical elements feel dated.

citations.review_text: Skyrim has an atmosphere that draws you back. The scenery, although dated, is still beautiful and the NPC's are a lot of fun to interact with. The dungeons can be cruel and brutal, but a challenge is always welcome. You can get lost in the crafting of potions, gardening, making weapons and armor or just adventuring around the map. The combat feels genuine if a little clunky at times, but it feels great to fell a dragon or clear hold of bandits. And the Draugr make for a great opponents in the cold murky depths of long ruined keeps. This is one of the greatest adventure games of all time. And it has a survival mode for the hardcore. So, pick a race, grab a weapon and get to Riverwood, for this adventure begins!
a true masterpiece. It is truly dated, both graphically and mechanically, but once spruced up with mods, it is second to none.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that updates and additions can break or destabilize existing mods.

citations.review_text: So, been playing this since elementary school, im now 24, and I have to admit, every year it feels like the game gets worse, less stable, and more bloated with paid mods no one asked for. I use to be able to claim this game was one of the best games in the world. Now I cant even say its the best game in the Bethesda roster. if you do want to play this game, your best bet is to play an older version of it and to block it's ability to update, so you can keep it frozen in the version that it actually functions in. Mods are constantly being broken at this point by 'additions' that really only take away from the game.

Greedy ass company trying to milk this 15 year old game by updating and bricking free mods for all users pushing paid Creation Club mods.

Embarassing and disgusting.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players encounter repetitive dungeons, weaker magic, and quest-blocking bugs.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the dungeons and crypts as highly repetitive in their game design.

citations.review_text:
[h1]If you owned the original steam release before Oct 28, 2016, then you got this for free. If you didn't, then too bad![/h1]

Do you know of the Elder Scrolls my homies? Have you heard of Skyrim!?

If you haven't, I shun you. You are unworthy.

Skyrim is such a popular game and is so well known, I shouldn't have to write a review - you should know everything about it already. Perhaps, then, I write more for developers of other games, instead of for potential gamers, because gamers shouldn't be reading reviews for this masterpiece, they should be paying / downloading / playing it.

So many game developers get things right, then go ahead and make a sequel and screw up everything everyone enjoyed about a game. It happens in almost every popular series - Final Fantasy is so different from I to XVI (and probably all the way up to M if the company survives long enough) they're completely different genres, Borderlands was great once but now it's thrashing a dead horse, and while I loved Diablo I and II I don't want anything to do with Blizzard any more.

So here is a game that got things right. Presenting... Skyrim!


____________

I could have ended the review right there and it would have been perfect. But as you well know, there is no such thing as a perfect game.

Some issues it has, regardless of whether it is the Special Edition or not, is the highly repetitive nature of the dungeons and crypts, weak magic compared to physical combat and weapons, shallow or weak questing (go fetch, or go kill this thing), and other things like over-simplified stats (what stats?, it's just skills, hp and stamina), and pointless dialogue choices.

Even with all those minor issues, the game is still ridiculously popular.

I have even come up with my own version of play, which is to start on maximum difficulty and drop the difficulty level every 20 levels. I think I've played the game to completion on various consoles and now multiple times on PC as well thanks to …

There's a lot of criticism that this game is a shallow RPG, that it dumbed down RPG elements that were in past elder scrolls games, you rarely make choices, the characters are bland, the combat is tedious, etc. Underneath all that, there's still an incredible open world to explore with soulful art and music, but all of that criticism is true. As fun as it is to explore Skyrim, the game really stops being interesting once you realize how repetitive its game design is. Honestly the best way to describe all the criticisms of Skyrim is that the game treats the player like an idiot. 

What you should really play this game for is the modding scene. Skyrim modding has gotten so advanced that you can essentially build your own RPG within Skyrim. You can practically make your own video game. That experience might honestly be some of the most fun I've had with PC gaming. You can turn this game into a survival RPG where you have to craft torches and food, or you can turn it into a third person action RPG. At this point you can genuinely make Skyrim whatever you want. It's something I recommend anyone with a good PC does at least once.

citations.review_text:
Seen many people say positive things about Skyrim before playing it. As a fan of magic, dragons, open world, and the idea of having followers; this game is an absolute blast. All of the quests are good, there are lots of factions I lead, and there are many marriage candidates even in the base game.

However, I do wish there were less bugs and crashes. It would also be nice if followers had more dialogue and quests like in Fallout 4. It would also be nice if they stopped saying "stupid dog" to Meeko.

[H1]“What is better - to be born good, or to overcome your evil nature through great effort?”
~ Paarthurnax[/H1]

A profound quote that really makes you think, Skyrim is more than just a game, for many people, it was an adventure of a lifetime.

I still remember the first time I discovered this universe, I was still in high school back then, it has been more than ten years now, and despite all that time, I still have nothing but good memories of this game every time I come back to it.

I started another playthrough in 2020, and the one I have just completed will be my last, I achieved everything I set out to do, I unlocked all the achievements, explored as much as possible, traveled across Skyrim and Solstheim, defeated Miraak, and helped countless people along the way.

I feel like I have left my own little mark on this world, and it has been an absolute pleasure despite the countless bugs the game has, some of which can be frustrating and even prevent you from progressing, but honestly, without those bugs, it would not quite be an Elder Scrolls game.

I am genuinely glad I got to experience this game, and I think everyone should play it at least once in their life, there really is no bad reason to say no, unless of course you simply hate The Elder Scrolls series.

Just do not buy it at full price, wait for a sale, like the one happening right now at around €10, at that price, it is absolutely worth it.

The game itself does not take up much space either, unless you are planning on building a massive modlist through MO2, personally, I just focused on giving the game a bit of a visual makeover, making it look a little better while bringing back that nostalgia from years ago, around 30 GB of mods to bring a chapter to a close.

Thank you, Skyrim. 🐉
